To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mass function in the Arches cluster is Salpeter-like down to about one solar mass, and that the Arches is about half-way toward core collapse.
the mass function in the Arches cluster can be explained as the result of the cluster’s evolution, without primordial mass-segregation.

(i) a Salpeter-like mass function is expected in the central regions of young and dense star-clusters, (ii) the Arches cluster is about half way towards core collapse, (iii) primordial mass segregation is not required to explain the Arches mass-function, and (iv) the mass function in the core of the Arches can be used to constrain the initial mass function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of young star clusters and their mass functions.
the evolution of the stellar initial mass function (IMF) in young and dense stellar systems.
the formation of the initial mass function in dense young clusters, and with the evolution of the cluster itself.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Arches mass distribution is consistent with a primordial Salpeter-like distribution and that the flattening of the mass function is a consequence of the dynamical evolution of a dense cluster.
the mass function is Salpeter-like down to 1 M⊙ and the flattening is caused by the dynamical evolution.
the Arches mass spectrum is consistent with a universal Salpeter mass spectrum down to ∼2 M⊙, but with a possible flattening at higher masses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mass functions for high-mass stars are not universal, but depend on the cluster’s dynamical state.
the Arches mass distribution can be explained as the result of a combination of the initial mass function, the dynamical evolution of the cluster and the mass loss by stellar evolution.
the mass function is determined by two factors, the initial mass function and the evolution of the cluster.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mass functions of young star clusters are expected to evolve with time.
the Arches mass spectrum can be understood in terms of a standard initial mass function and a cluster with an intermediate dynamical age.
the mass segregation is not the only explanation for the peculiarities observed in the Arches cluster mass function.
